analysis:
At AIMA's 10th National Leadership Conclave on 15 April 2025, Road Transport and Highways Minister Nitin Gadkari said India's road infrastructure would surpass that of the United States within 18 months, and separately set a highway-construction goal of 100 km per day.

PIB and MoRTH data report National Highways at about 1,46,560 km and describe India as having the world's second-largest road network. Comparative data place the United States' total road network at about 6.6 million km against India's about 6.4 million km. In FY 2024-25, National Highway construction ran at about 29 km per day, against the 100 km per day goal.

Because the statement does not specify a measurable benchmark for 'surpass' and mixes network length, quality and construction pace, the outcome cannot be scored against a single metric; it is recorded as unverifiable.
notes: Gadkari has made similar 'better than the US' statements on several dates (March 2025, April 2025 for Madhya Pradesh, June 2025); this entry uses the 15 April 2025 AIMA statement, which carries the 18-month window. Quotation is reported wording, not a transcript, so not marked verbatim. Comparative road-length figures come from a secondary compilation, not a government source, and are used only for context.
